title: Sync/reopen/close/comment endpoints reject a bug report ID belonging to another organization
description: Every mutating action (syncBugReportStatus, reopenBugReport, closeBugReport, getComments, addComment) independently checks `String(report.organizationId) === String(req.orgId)` and throws 403 'Access denied' before any ownership/permission check runs — this must hold even for a valid, well-formed ObjectId that simply belongs to a different tenant.
preconditions: Org A and Org B each have a bug report
Valid JWT for a user in Org A
steps: As an Org A user, call POST /bug-reports/:id/sync using Org B's report _id
expectedResult: All five requests return 403 'Access denied' — no field from Org B's report (description, jiraKey, comments) is present in any response body.
requirement: OWASP API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization

title: A non-creator without bug-report.read_all cannot view, sync, reopen, close, or comment on another user's report in the same org
description: The ownership check `String(report.userId) !== String(req.userId) && !canReadAll(req)` gates every single-report action. A regular user (no read_all) targeting a co-worker's ticket in the same organization/project must be blocked identically to the cross-org case, distinguishing horizontal privilege escalation within a tenant from IDOR across tenants.
preconditions: User A and User B in the same org; User B has no bug-report.read_all; User A owns a bug report
steps: As User B, call POST /bug-reports/:id/reopen and /:id/close on User A's report id
As User B, call GET /:id/comments and POST /:id/comments on the same report id
expectedResult: All four requests return 403 'Access denied'. The response does not leak whether the resource exists vs. is merely inaccessible (same generic message and status as the cross-org case in SUPP-SEC-001).

title: Jira webhook uses timing-safe comparison and rejects mismatched or missing secrets
description: jiraWebhook() compares Buffer.from(expectedSecret) against Buffer.from(receivedSecret) with crypto.timingSafeEqual only after confirming equal length (timingSafeEqual throws on length mismatch, so the length check must run first) — this guards against a timing side-channel on secret comparison, unlike a naive === check.
preconditions: JIRA_WEBHOOK_SECRET is configured with a known value
steps: POST /bug-reports/webhook/jira?secret=<wrong-value-same-length> with a valid webhookEvent payload
POST /bug-reports/webhook/jira with no secret query param at all
expectedResult: All three requests return 401 'Unauthorized' (or 'Webhook not configured' if unset) and no BugReport document is read or modified; response timing does not leak how many leading characters of the secret matched.

title: Webhook fails closed (401) when JIRA_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured, rather than accepting unauthenticated requests
description: `if (!expectedSecret) return res.status(401).json({success:false, message:'Webhook not configured'})` runs before any secret comparison — an operator forgetting to set the secret must not accidentally leave the webhook open to arbitrary status-changing requests from the internet.
steps: POST /bug-reports/webhook/jira?secret=anything with a well-formed jira:issue_updated payload targeting a real jiraKey
expectedResult: 401 'Webhook not configured' is returned and the targeted report's status/jiraStatusRaw is unchanged in the database.

title: Webhook silently ignores non-issue_updated events and updates for an untracked Jira key
description: jiraWebhook() only processes req.body.webhookEvent === 'jira:issue_updated'; any other event type returns {received:true} without touching the database. Likewise, a jiraKey that doesn't match any BugReport returns {received:true} with a warning log — an attacker who guesses/enumerates jiraKey values with a valid secret cannot use the webhook to discover which keys exist in this tenant's data via a differing response.
preconditions: Valid JIRA_WEBHOOK_SECRET known to the caller
steps: POST the webhook with webhookEvent:'jira:issue_created' and a valid secret
POST the webhook with webhookEvent:'jira:issue_updated' and an issue.key that does not match any BugReport
expectedResult: Both requests return 200 {received:true} with an identical response shape — no information about which jiraKeys exist is inferable from the response.

title: GET /bug-reports/all cannot be reached by directly calling the API even if a user manipulates client-side state to force the All Tickets tab
description: requirePermission('bug-report.read_all') is enforced as Express middleware on the route itself, independent of the frontend's canReadAll gate — this closes the gap where a user could otherwise use browser devtools to flip local component state and call the underlying service function directly.
steps: Using devtools or a direct HTTP client (bypassing the React UI entirely), call GET /bug-reports/all with the user's own valid JWT
expectedResult: 403 is returned by the requirePermission middleware before listAllBugReports executes — no cross-user ticket data from the org is returned.

title: Organization isolation is enforced even for a superadmin/read_all holder — the org check runs before the ownership/permission bypass
description: In every handler (sync/reopen/close/getComments/addComment), the `sameOrg` check throws 403 unconditionally before canReadAll()/isSuperAdmin() is ever consulted for ownership. A user with bug-report.read_all (or a superadmin role) can bypass the *ownership* check within their own org, but must never bypass the *organizationId* boundary itself.
preconditions: A user in Org A holding bug-report.read_all (or superadmin)
A bug report belonging to Org B
steps: As the Org A read_all/superadmin user, call GET /bug-reports/:id/comments using Org B's report id
Compare against the same user calling the same route with an Org A report id owned by a different Org A user
expectedResult: The Org B request is rejected with 403 regardless of read_all/superadmin status; the Org A request (different owner, same org) succeeds because read_all legitimately bypasses only the ownership check, not the tenant boundary.

title: Bug report description containing script/HTML payload is not executed when rendered in the ticket detail drawer
description: The description is stored verbatim (trimmed) in MongoDB and also sent to Jira as ADF plain text (buildAdf wraps it in a {type:'text', text: ...} node, not raw HTML), so no markup interpretation happens on the Jira side either. The client panel renders selectedTicket.description inside a plain Chakra <Box> (React default-escapes text content), not via dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
steps: Submit a bug report with description: '<script>alert(1)</script> Steps to reproduce: 20+ chars of padding text here'
Open the created ticket's detail drawer in the client panel
Inspect the Jira issue's description field
expectedResult: The drawer renders the literal text '<script>alert(1)</script> ...' with no script execution; the Jira issue description shows the same literal text inside its ADF text node, not as an executed/rendered HTML element.
